story.label: OUR STORY
story.title: Born from a passion for African nature
story.p1: The Biodiversity and Environment Care Organisation (BECO) is an independent, apolitical, non-profit organisation, founded in 2025 in Yaoundé, Cameroon. Founded by Dr SIMEU NOUTCHOM Alain and a team of passionate young researchers, BECO was born from a simple observation: African biodiversity, among the richest in the world, is threatened like never before.
story.p2: Faced with ecosystem degradation, habitat loss and the effects of climate change, we chose action. Our approach combines rigorous scientific research, community engagement and technological innovation to create sustainable solutions adapted to the African context.
story.p3: Today, BECO carries out several active projects in Cameroon, mobilises a network of international partners and trains the next generation of African conservationists.

news.label: OUR NEWS
news.title: Stay informed about our work
fullContent:
BECO has officially launched its new conservation programme dedicated to protecting African grey parrots (Psittacus erithacus) in Mpem & Djim National Park. This project, supported by the 1Wild Foundation, aims to halt the decline of this emblematic species threatened by illegal trade and habitat loss.

The programme includes several components: scientific monitoring of populations through counts and direct observations, raising awareness among local communities about the importance of protecting the species, combating poaching and illegal trafficking, as well as mapping priority nesting areas.

BECO teams are already in the field deploying the first actions of this ambitious programme that will span several years.

The British Ecological Society (BES) has selected BECO's project entitled "Acoustic variability of Orthoptera in response to climate variables along the Cameroon Volcanic Line" for funding. This grant will enable our organisation to conduct an in-depth study on the impact of climate change on Orthoptera communities.

The project will use automated acoustic recorders deployed at several sites at different altitudes along the Cameroon Volcanic Line. The collected data will be correlated with climate variables to model the impacts of climate change on these insect populations, which are excellent bioindicators of ecosystem health.

This project represents a significant advance for acoustic ecology research in Central Africa and strengthens BECO's position as a player in scientific research for conservation.

BECO has received its second Rufford Small Grant (no. 48049-2) to continue passive acoustic monitoring of Orthoptera in Mpem & Djim National Park. After a conclusive first phase, this second funding will expand the spatial and temporal coverage of the monitoring.

Orthoptera (grasshoppers and crickets) are key indicators of ecosystem health. Their diversity and abundance provide information on the conservation status of habitats. Using acoustic sensors deployed in different park habitats, BECO researchers can identify species present and assess biodiversity non-invasively.

A reference acoustic database will be created, providing a valuable resource for future research and conservation actions in the region.

Our Executive Director, Dr SIMEU NOUTCHOM Alain, has been selected as a fellow of the CDKN (Climate and Development Knowledge Network) programme for early-career African researchers. This prestigious programme aims to support the next generation of African scientists working on climate change issues.

Dr SIMEU NOUTCHOM Alain will benefit from personalised mentoring, funding for his research project and networking opportunities with other African researchers. He will join a community of fellows committed to advancing climate research across the continent.

This recognition testifies to the quality of BECO's work and its commitment to training tomorrow's scientific talent.

The Biodiversity and Environment Care Organisation (BECO) has been officially founded and registered in Yaoundé, Cameroon, by a group of passionate young researchers. Founded by Dr SIMEU NOUTCHOM Alain, the organisation was born from a simple observation: African biodiversity, among the richest in the world, is threatened like never before.

Based in Yaoundé, BECO's mission is to promote biodiversity conservation, environmental sustainability, climate change mitigation and adaptation, sustainable agriculture, public health and community empowerment.

From its creation, the BECO team mobilised to launch the first research and conservation projects, notably in Mpem & Djim National Park, laying the foundations for an organisation set to play a major role in biodiversity conservation in Central Africa.

The first data collected as part of the Orthoptera acoustic monitoring project in Mpem & Djim National Park reveal a remarkable richness of the Orthoptera community present in the park. The recordings made by acoustic sensors deployed in different habitats show an unsuspected diversity of species.

Preliminary analyses indicate the presence of numerous species of grasshoppers and crickets, some of which may be new to science or never before documented in this region of Cameroon. These results confirm the importance of Mpem & Djim National Park as a biodiversity refuge.

BECO plans to publish these results in an international scientific journal, contributing to the knowledge and conservation of Cameroonian biodiversity.

faq.label: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS
faq.title: Everything you need to know
faq.description: Find answers to the most common questions about BECO, our activities and how to get involved.
faq.a1: BECO (Biodiversity and Environment Care Organisation) is a non-governmental, apolitical, non-profit organisation founded in 2025 in Yaoundé, Cameroon, working for biodiversity conservation and environmental protection.
faq.q2: How can I become a member of BECO?
faq.a2: BECO offers three membership categories: Active Member, Institutional Member and Honorary Member. Visit our 'Get Involved' page to choose the plan that suits you.
faq.q3: How can I make a donation?
faq.a3: You can make a donation via our 'Get Involved' page which offers different amounts (10,000 FCFA, 25,000 FCFA, 50,000 FCFA or a custom amount). Each donation entitles you to a tax receipt.
faq.a4: BECO is based in Yaoundé, Cameroon, and carries out its projects mainly in Cameroon and Central Africa.
faq.a5: Go to our 'Get Involved' page and fill in the volunteer form. We are looking for volunteers for fieldwork, research, environmental education and communication.
faq.a6: Yes, BECO regularly welcomes interns as part of its programmes. Contact us via our Contact page.
faq.a7: You can contact us by email at beco@afrotropical.org, by phone at +237 6 57 90 27 84, or via our online contact form.
faq.q8: Does BECO work with international partners?
faq.a8: Yes, BECO collaborates with several partners including the Rufford Foundation, 1Wild Foundation, MBZ Species Conservation Fund, IDEA WILD, the British Ecological Society and CDKN.
